title: The Riemann Zeta Function
description: Basel values, analytic continuation, infinite series and Mellin integrals, interactive critical-strip spirals, and domain coloring of non-trivial zeros.
markdown:
# The Riemann Zeta Function

For $s > 1$, the Riemann zeta function $zeta(s) = 1 + 2^(-s) + 3^(-s) + 4^(-s)$ (summed over all $n >= 1$) extends meromorphically across the complex plane with a single simple pole at $s = 1$.

## 1. The Basel Problem & Even Integers

Euler proved that all even positive integers evaluate to rational multiples of powers of $pi$, whereas odd integers such as Apery's constant $zeta(3)$ are evaluated numerically:

```math
zeta(2)
```

```math
zeta(4)
```

```math
zeta(6)
```

```math
zeta(8)
```

```math
approx(zeta(3))
```

Exact values: $zeta(2)$ = {{r[1]}}, $zeta(4)$ = {{r[2]}}, $zeta(6)$ = {{r[3]}}, $zeta(8)$ = {{r[4]}}, and numerically $zeta(3)$ ≈ {{r[5]}}.

## 2. Analytic Continuation & Trivial Zeros

Across Riemann's functional reflection equation, negative integers map cleanly to rational Bernoulli values, vanishing at all negative even integers:

```math
zeta(0)
```

```math
zeta(-1)
```

```math
zeta(-2)
```

```math
zeta(-3)
```

```math
zeta(-5)
```

Thus $zeta(0)$ = {{r[6]}}, Ramanujan's regularized sum `1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + ...` gives $zeta(-1)$ = {{r[7]}}, the first trivial zero sits at $zeta(-2)$ = {{r[8]}}, while $zeta(-3)$ = {{r[9]}} and $zeta(-5)$ = {{r[10]}}.

## 3. Infinite Series, Mellin Integral & Numerical Verification

Define the Bose-Einstein integrand $bose(x) = x / (exp(x) - 1)$ once so both Dirichlet summation and Mellin integration agree with $zeta(2)$ = {{r[1]}} and $zeta(4)$ = {{r[2]}}:

```math
bose(x) := x / (exp(x) - 1)
```

```math
sum(1 / n^2, n, 1..infinity)
```

```math
sum(1 / n^4, n, 1..infinity)
```

```math
integrate(bose(x), x, 0..infinity)
```

```math
nintegrate(bose(x), x, 0.0001..25)
```

Symbolic Mellin integration returns {{r[14]}} alongside adaptive quadrature {{r[15]}}.

## 4. Parametric Spirals Along the Critical Strip

Sweep $sigma$ across the critical strip `0..1` (defaulting to the critical line `Re(s) = 1/2`) via $zline(t) = zeta(sigma + i*t)$ to explore how the trajectory `(Re ζ(σ + it), Im ζ(σ + it))` spirals through the complex plane. Along `Re(s) = 1/2`, every loop passing through the origin marks a non-trivial zero of the Riemann hypothesis:

```math
sigma := slider(0..1, default: 0.5, step: 0.01, label: 'real part σ')
```

```math
zline(t) := zeta(sigma + i*t)
```

```math
parametric(re(zline(t)), im(zline(t)), t, t: 0..34, title: 'ζ(σ + it) Critical-Strip Spiral (t: 0..34)')
```

Plotting $re(zline(t))$, $im(zline(t))$, and $abs(zline(t))$ against $t$ pinpoints the simultaneous zero crossings at $t$ ≈ 14.135, 21.022, 25.011, and 30.425 when $sigma = 0.5$:

```math
plot([re(zline(t)), im(zline(t)), abs(zline(t))], t, x: 0..34, title: 'Re, Im & |ζ(σ + it)| Along Re(s) = σ')
```

## 5. Complex Plane & The Critical Strip

In OKLCH domain coloring, zeros appear as rainbow phase vortices converging on black points (such as the trivial zeros at negative even integers and the first three non-trivial zeros along `Re(z) = 1/2`), while the pole at $z = 1$ flares white:

```math
plotcomplex(zeta(z), z, re: -6..4, im: -26..26, title: 'Complex Domain Coloring of ζ(z)')
```

Verify the first two non-trivial zeros numerically:

```math
zeta(0.5 + 14.1347251417*i)
```

```math
zeta(0.5 + 21.0220396388*i)
```

## 6. 3D Analytic Modulus Landscape

Finally, view the modulus landscape $abs(zeta(z))$ colored by phase angle across the pole and critical strip:

```math
plotcomplex3d(zeta(z), z, re: -3..3, im: -16..16, title: 'Analytic Landscape |ζ(z)|')
```

title: Damped Oscillator & Phase Portraits
description: Interactive underdamped kinematics, higher-order derivatives, exact differential equation solutions, high-resolution ODE curves, and phase-space vector fields.
markdown:
# Damped Oscillator & Phase Portraits

Adjust damping $gamma$ and angular frequency $omega$ to explore the underdamped oscillation $f(t) = exp(-gamma * t) * sin(omega * t)$ for $t >= 0$:

```math
gamma := slider(0.05..1, default: 0.2, step: 0.05, label: 'damping γ');
omega := slider(0.5..5, default: 2, step: 0.25, label: 'frequency ω');
```

```math
env(t) := exp(-gamma * t)
```

```math
f(t) := env(t) * sin(omega * t)
```

## Velocity, Acceleration & Extrema

Compute instantaneous velocity and second-order acceleration symbolically:

```math
diff(f(t), t)
```

```math
diff(f(t), t, order: 2)
```

With live interpolation, the velocity is $v(t)$ = {{r[4]}}. Locate the first peak numerically over `0..pi/omega`:

```math
nsolve(diff(f(t), t) = 0, t, range: 0..pi/omega)
```

Plot the displaced curve bounded within its exponential decay envelope:

```math
plot([f(t), env(t), -env(t)], t, x: 0..12, title: 'Damped Oscillation & Envelope')
```

## Exact & Numerical Differential Equations

Vary decay rate $mu$ and solve the harmonically forced first-order ODE both analytically via `dsolve` and numerically via dense Hermite interpolation:

```math
mu := slider(0.1..1.5, default: 0.4, step: 0.05, label: 'decay rate μ')
```

```math
dsolve(D(y, t) + mu * y = cos(t), y, t)
```

```math
ode(-mu * y + cos(t), y, t, y0: 1, t: 0..14, title: 'Forced Decay Solution')
```

## Damped Pendulum Phase Portrait

Vary friction $c$ to inspect the phase plane `(x, y)` = `(θ, θ')` around stable spiral attractors and saddle separatrices:

```math
c := slider(0..1.5, default: 0.3, step: 0.05, label: 'friction c')
```

```math
vectorfield(y, -sin(x) - c * y, x, y, x: -5..5, y: -3..3, title: 'Damped Pendulum Phase Portrait')
```

title: Complex Singularities & Conformal Maps
description: Interactive root order $n$, complex polynomial roots, rational zero-pole topology, essential singularities, Joukowsky conformal mapping, and Euler identities.
markdown:
# Complex Singularities & Conformal Maps

Every non-constant polynomial factors completely over the complex numbers. Define $p(z) = z^4 + 4$, solve $p(z) = 0$, and verify its factored conjugate pairs:

```math
p(z) := z^4 + 4
```

```math
solve(p(z) = 0, z)
```

```math
factor(p(z))
```

## Zeros, Poles & Essential Singularities

Sweep the root order $n$ of $w(z) = (z^n - 1)/(z^2 + 1)$ to watch $n$ zeros orbit the unit circle around the simple poles at $i$ and $-i$:

```math
n := slider(2..6, default: 3, step: 1, label: 'root order n')
```

```math
w(z) := (z^n - 1)/(z^2 + 1)
```

```math
plotcomplex(w(z), z, re: -2.5..2.5, im: -2.5..2.5, title: 'Zeros and Poles of w(z)')
```

Contrast simple poles with the essential singularity of $exp(1/z)$ at $z = 0$, where every neighborhood omits at most one value:

```math
plotcomplex(exp(1/z), z, re: -1.5..1.5, im: -1.5..1.5, title: 'Essential Singularity exp(1/z)')
```

## Conformal Joukowsky Transformation & 3D Landscape

The Joukowsky airfoil map $j(z) = z + 1/z$ maps circles onto ellipses and airfoils:

```math
j(z) := z + 1/z
```

```math
plotcomplex(j(z), z, re: -2.5..2.5, im: -2.5..2.5, title: 'Joukowsky Conformal Map j(z) = z + 1/z')
```

Visualize $abs(1/(z^n - 1))$ as a 3D analytic modulus landscape driven by $n$:

```math
plotcomplex3d(1/(z^n - 1), z, re: -2..2, im: -2..2, title: 'Modulus Surface |1/(z^n - 1)|')
```

## Exponential & Hyperbolic Rewrites

```math
rewrite(sin(x)^2 + cos(x)^2, 'exp')
```

```math
simplify(r[-1])
```

title: Multivariable Calculus & Surfaces
description: Symbolic gradients, Hessians, Jacobians, shared surface and contour functions, 3D vector fields, and interactive Lissajous curves.
markdown:
# Multivariable Calculus & Surfaces

Define a smooth two-variable Gaussian saddle potential $V(x, y)$ once and reuse it across symbolic operators and plots:

```math
V(x, y) := (x^2 - y^2) * exp(-(x^2 + y^2) / 4)
```

## Gradient, Hessian & Polar Jacobian

Compute the gradient vector field and Hessian matrix of second partial derivatives at `(x, y)`:

```math
gradient(V(x, y), [x, y])
```

```math
hessian(V(x, y), [x, y])
```

Verify the area element `r` of polar coordinates via the Jacobian determinant:

```math
det(jacobian([r * cos(theta), r * sin(theta)], [r, theta]))
```

```math
simplify(r[-1])
```

## 3D Surface, Scalar Heatmap & 3D Vector Field

Render the 3D potential surface alongside its contour heatmap and a rotational 3D curl field:

```math
plot3d(V(x, y), x, y, x: -3.5..3.5, y: -3.5..3.5, title: 'Gaussian Saddle Surface')
```

```math
heatmap(V(x, y), x, y, x: -3.5..3.5, y: -3.5..3.5, title: 'Potential Contours')
```

```math
vectorfield3d(-y, x, 0.25 * z, x, y, z, x: -2..2, y: -2..2, grid: 5, title: '3D Swirling Flow Field')
```

## Interactive Parametric Lissajous Projection

Vary integer harmonic frequencies $p$ and $q$ to morph the Lissajous knot:

```math
p := slider(1..7, default: 3, step: 1, label: 'x-frequency p');
q := slider(1..7, default: 4, step: 1, label: 'y-frequency q');
```

```math
parametric(sin(p * t), sin(q * t), t, t: 0..2*pi, title: 'Lissajous Curve')
```

title: Linear Algebra & Spectral Analysis
description: Matrix inverses, determinants, characteristic polynomials, exact eigenvalues, Cayley-Hamilton theorem, RREF, and linear systems.
markdown:
# Linear Algebra & Spectral Analysis

Define a symmetric 2×2 matrix $A$ and inspect its trace, determinant, transpose, and exact inverse:

```math
A := [[5, 2], [2, 2]]
```

```math
trace(A)
```

```math
det(A)
```

```math
inv(A)
```

With determinant {{r[3]}} and trace {{r[2]}}, the inverse is {{r[4]}}.

## Characteristic Polynomial & Cayley-Hamilton

Compute the characteristic polynomial and exact eigenvalues of $A$:

```math
charpoly(A, lambda)
```

```math
eigenvals(A)
```

Verify the Cayley-Hamilton theorem directly by substituting $A$ into $A^2 - trace(A) * A + det(A) * I$:

```math
A * A - trace(A) * A + det(A) * [[1, 0], [0, 1]]
```

## 3×3 Rank & Coupled Linear Systems

Inspect row-reduced echelon form and solve a coupled 3×3 system simultaneously:

```math
rref([[1, 2, -1, 3], [2, -1, 3, 7], [-1, 1, 2, 4]])
```

```math
solvesystem([x + 2*y - z = 3, 2*x - y + 3*z = 7, -x + y + 2*z = 4], [x, y, z])
```

Verify a 3×3 matrix product with its inverse:

```math
B := [[2, 1, 0], [1, 3, 1], [0, 1, 2]]
```

```math
B * inv(B)
```

title: Integrals, Asymptotics & Series
description: Indefinite antiderivatives, definite and Gaussian improper integrals, interactive Taylor approximations, limits, and closed-form sums and products.
markdown:
# Integrals, Asymptotics & Series

Explore symbolic integration, Gaussian quadrature, interactive Taylor approximations, limits, and discrete sums.

## Indefinite, Definite & Improper Integrals

```math
integrate(x^2 * exp(-x), x)
```

```math
integrate(x * sin(x), x, 0..pi)
```

Define the Gaussian bell $g(x) = exp(-x^2)$ once and evaluate its improper integral on `-infinity..infinity` alongside finite numerical truncation:

```math
g(x) := exp(-x^2)
```

```math
integrate(g(x), x, -infinity..infinity)
```

```math
nintegrate(g(x), x, -5..5)
```

Exact improper integral: {{r[4]}}, numerical truncation over `-5..5`: {{r[5]}}.

## Interactive Taylor Polynomials

Enter any smooth expression $f(x)$ and vary the polynomial degree to inspect its Maclaurin series and overlay partial sums graphically:

```math
f := input(cos(x), label: 'function f(x)');
deg := slider(2..10, default: 6, step: 2, label: 'Taylor order');
```

```math
taylor(f, x, order: deg)
```

```math
series(exp(x) * sin(x), x, order: 5)
```

```math
plot([f, taylor(f, x, order: 2), taylor(f, x, order: 4), taylor(f, x, order: deg)], x, x: -3.2..3.2, title: 'Taylor Approximations of f(x)')
```

## Limits, Summations & Products

```math
limit((exp(x) - 1 - x) / x^2, x, 0)
```

```math
sum(k^3, k, 1..n)
```

```math
product((k + 1) / k, k, 1..n)
```

title: Orthogonal Polynomials & Special Functions
description: Interactive Legendre and Chebyshev order explorer, orthogonality integrals, Bessel oscillations, and Gamma/Beta identities.
markdown:
# Orthogonal Polynomials & Special Functions

Explore classical orthogonal polynomials interactively in degree $n$ and verify exact $L^2$ orthogonality.

## Legendre & Chebyshev Families

Adjust degree $n$ to inspect the Legendre polynomial $P_n(x)$ and Chebyshev polynomial $T_n(x)$ side-by-side:

```math
n := slider(0..8, default: 3, step: 1, label: 'order n')
```

```math
legendreP(n, x)
```

```math
chebyshevT(n, x)
```

Legendre polynomials are mutually orthogonal on `-1..1`:

```math
integrate(legendreP(2, x) * legendreP(3, x), x, -1..1)
```

```math
integrate(legendreP(3, x)^2, x, -1..1)
```

Compare $P_n(x)$ and $T_n(x)$ graphically on `-1..1`:

```math
plot([legendreP(n, x), chebyshevT(n, x)], x, x: -1..1, title: 'Legendre Pₙ(x) vs. Chebyshev Tₙ(x)')
```

## Bessel Functions & Gamma / Beta Values

Compare cylindrical Bessel waves $besselJ(0, x)$, $besselJ(1, x)$, and $besselJ(2, x)$:

```math
plot([besselJ(0, x), besselJ(1, x), besselJ(2, x)], x, x: 0..15, title: 'Bessel Functions of the First Kind')
```

Verify exact values of the Euler Gamma and Beta functions:

```math
gamma(1/2)
```

```math
beta(3, 4)
```

```math
approx(erf(1))
```

title: Fourier Synthesis & Wave Interference
description: Square-wave partial Fourier sums, orthogonality integrals, interactive acoustic beat envelopes, and 2D standing drumhead modes.
markdown:
# Fourier Synthesis & Wave Interference

Approximate a $2 * pi$-periodic odd square wave via odd harmonics $4/pi * sin(k * x)/k$:

```math
sq3(x) := (4 / pi) * (sin(x) + sin(3*x)/3 + sin(5*x)/5)
```

```math
sq5(x) := sq3(x) + (4 / pi) * (sin(7*x)/7 + sin(9*x)/9)
```

Plot the progressive Fourier partial sums over `-pi..pi` to observe the characteristic Gibbs overshoot near discontinuities:

```math
plot([4/pi * sin(x), sq3(x), sq5(x)], x, x: -pi..pi, title: 'Fourier Square-Wave Partial Sums')
```

Verify exact Fourier harmonic orthogonality over `0..2*pi`:

```math
integrate(sin(2 * x) * sin(3 * x), x, 0..2*pi)
```

```math
integrate(sin(3 * x)^2, x, 0..2*pi)
```

## Interactive Beat Interference & 2D Drumhead Mode

Tune nearby wave frequencies $f_1$ and $f_2$ to see amplitude modulation beats within `±env(x)`:

```math
f1 := slider(6..14, default: 10, step: 0.5, label: 'frequency f₁');
f2 := slider(6..14, default: 11, step: 0.5, label: 'frequency f₂');
```

```math
beat(x) := sin(f1 * x) + sin(f2 * x)
```

```math
env(x) := 2 * cos((f2 - f1) * x / 2)
```

```math
plot([beat(x), env(x), -env(x)], x, x: 0..4*pi, title: 'Acoustic Beat Modulation')
```

Select integer eigenmode numbers `(m, n)` to visualize a clamped rectangular membrane in 3D:

```math
m := slider(1..5, default: 2, step: 1, label: 'mode m');
n := slider(1..5, default: 3, step: 1, label: 'mode n');
```

```math
mode(x, y) := sin(m * x) * sin(n * y)
```

```math
plot3d(mode(x, y), x, y, x: 0..pi, y: 0..pi, title: '2D Standing Membrane Mode (m, n)')
```

# Number Theory, Primes & Combinatorics

Explore integer prime factorization, divisibility, exact rational reconstruction, and combinatorial closed forms.

## Interactive Integer Factorization & Primality

Enter any integer $n$ to inspect its prime factorization and primality status live:

```math
n := input(2520, label: 'integer n')
```

```math
factor(n)
```

```math
isprime(n)
```

## Divisibility, Modular Arithmetic & Rationals

```math
gcd(840, 1260, 1512)
```

```math
lcm(18, 24, 30)
```

```math
mod(2^10, 97)
```

```math
exact(0.375 * x + 1.25)
```

Here $gcd(840, 1260, 1512)$ = {{r[4]}}, $lcm(18, 24, 30)$ = {{r[5]}}, while for {{r[1]}} we obtain prime factorization {{r[2]}} and primality {{r[3]}}.

## Algebraic Golden Ratio & Combinatorics

Solve the golden ratio quadratic $phi^2 - phi - 1 = 0$ exactly:

```math
solve(phi^2 - phi - 1 = 0, phi)
```

Compute exact binomial coefficients and compare logarithmic growth of $ln(x!)$ against Stirling's asymptotic approximation on `1..12`:

```math
binomial(12, 5)
```

```math
plot([ln(gamma(x + 1)), x * ln(x) - x + 1/2 * ln(2 * pi * x)], x, x: 1..12, title: 'Log-Factorial vs. Stirling Approximation')
```

## Geometric & Harmonic Sums

```math
sum(1 / 2^k, k, 0..infinity)
```

```math
sum(k * (k + 1), k, 1..m)
```

title: Optimization, Root Finding & Curves
description: Symbolic critical points, numerical minimization, transcendental roots, nonlinear systems, interactive epicycloids, and Rosenbrock contours.
markdown:
# Optimization, Root Finding & Curves

Combine symbolic differentiation with high-precision numerical solvers across 1D and 2D problems.

## Symbolic Extrema & Numerical Minimization

Analyze the quartic double-well potential $f(x) = x^4 - 4 * x^2 + x$:

```math
f(x) := x^4 - 4 * x^2 + x
```

```math
solve(diff(f(x), x) = 0, x)
```

Locate the global minimum numerically with Brent's method on `-3..0`, and plot the double-well landscape:

```math
nminimize(f(x), x, range: -3..0)
```

```math
plot(f(x), x, x: -2.5..2.5, title: 'Asymmetric Double-Well Potential')
```

## Transcendental Roots & Nonlinear Systems

Solve the classic fixed-point equation $cos(x) = x$ and intersect a circle with a hyperbola via multivariate Newton-Raphson:

```math
nsolve(cos(x) = x, x, range: 0..1)
```

```math
nsolvesystem([x^2 + y^2 - 5, x * y - 2], [x, y], [2, 1])
```

```math
nderivative(exp(sin(x)), x, 0)
```

## Interactive Epicycloid Curve & Rosenbrock Contours

Vary the radius ratio $k$ to generate $(k - 1)$-cusped epicycloids alongside the classical curved valley of the Rosenbrock function:

```math
k := slider(2..8, default: 4, step: 1, label: 'epicycloid ratio k')
```

```math
epx(t) := k * cos(t) - cos(k * t)
```

```math
epy(t) := k * sin(t) - sin(k * t)
```

```math
parametric(epx(t), epy(t), t, t: 0..2*pi, title: 'Epicycloid Curve')
```

```math
rosenbrock(x, y) := (1 - x)^2 + 20 * (y - x^2)^2
```

```math
heatmap(rosenbrock(x, y), x, y, x: -2..2, y: -1..3, title: 'Rosenbrock Valley Heatmap')
```

# Interactive Wave & Formula Explorer

Adjust any slider or formula input below — dependent formulas, prose interpolations, and graphs recompute automatically in topological order.

## Parameters

```math
a := slider(-2..2, default: 1, step: 0.1, label: 'amplitude a');
w := slider(1..8, default: 2, step: 0.5, label: 'frequency w');
```

```math
b := input(pi / 4, label: 'phase shift b')
```

## Dependent Symbolic Form & Derivative

Define $f(x) = a * sin(w * x + b)$ once so symbolic outputs, derivatives, and plots share the same expression:

```math
f(x) := a * sin(w * x + b)
```

```math
f(x)
```

```math
diff(f(x), x)
```

Current wave formula $f(x)$ = {{r[4]}} with rate of change $diff(f(x), x)$ = {{r[5]}}.

## Live Reactive Plots

```math
plot([f(x), a * cos(w * x + b)], x, x: -pi..pi, title: 'Harmonic Wave & Quadrature')
```

```math
parametric(a * cos(w * t), cos(w * t + b), t, t: 0..2*pi, title: 'Lissajous Phase Ellipse')
```
